title: Claude Haiku vs Sonnet vs Opus: Which Model Saves Time & Money?

heroes.title: It is time to use AI smarter.
Your token budget — where it goes.

bodies:
function(){return '

Most professionals use Claude every day — but almost everyone defaults to the most powerful (and heaviest) model for every single task, even when a lighter one would do the job just as well.

This mini-course gives you a clear, practical framework for choosing the right Claude model every time, so you stop burning your daily usage limit on tasks that do not need it.

What you will learn: the difference between Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus — and a simple rule to pick the right one in under 10 seconds.

';}

function(){return '

Claude has three main models. Each is more capable — and heavier on your daily usage limit — than the last. The numbers below are relative weights, not per-message charges.

Haiku 4.5
1×
Fastest. Best for simple, high-volume tasks: drafting, classifying, routing, summarising.
Recommended default
Sonnet 4.6
3×
The smart default for most professional work — reports, briefs, analysis, emails.
Opus 4.7
5×
Most powerful. Reserve for complex reasoning, strategy, and high-stakes outputs only.

Note: API pricing for developers is different from subscription plan limits. Do not confuse the two — they work differently.

';}

function(){return '

Every conversation has a token budget. It comes from three sources — and all of them are within your control to manage.

Your input
Everything you type, paste, or upload. The biggest variable you control.
System context
Project instructions and background context loaded automatically.
Model output
Claude\'s responses. Longer outputs consume more of your daily budget.

The 10-second rule: before every conversation ask — does this need deep reasoning or fast execution? Fast execution goes to Haiku or Sonnet. Deep reasoning goes to Sonnet or Opus. When in doubt, Sonnet is almost always the right default.

';}

quiz.q: Your team needs to draft 100 product descriptions. Which model should you use?
opts: Haiku — fast and efficient for volume work

quiz.q: You are writing a sensitive legal brief for a major client. Which model is most appropriate?
opts: Sonnet or Opus — complex, high-stakes task
They all produce the same output

quiz.q: On a Pro/Team plan, what happens when you use Opus for every task?
opts: Nothing — the plan covers unlimited use
You hit your daily usage limit faster
You get charged extra per message

quiz.q: Where does your token budget come from in a conversation?
opts: Only from the messages you type
From your input, system context, and model output combined
